title: DARPA MXO Office-Wide BAA DARPA-PS-26-115
summary: MXO's office-wide announcement seeks revolutionary advances in science, devices, and integrated systems. Its remit extends from materials and components to tools, processes, architectures, and domestic supply chains that can scale foundational hardware.
key_findings: MXO is expanding beyond individual microsystems toward connected architectures and capabilities.
The research frame includes materials, fabrication tools, processes, components, and unconventional physical modalities.
Indigenous production tools and material supply chains are part of the technical problem.
why_it_matters: The BAA treats manufacturing sovereignty and supply-chain depth as requirements for strategic hardware advantage.
ftfn_relevance: Connects chips, advanced manufacturing, materials, and industrial tooling within one dependency stack.
Creates a watch lane for the transition from component breakthroughs to scalable domestic production systems.
evidence_limits: The opportunity describes desired research, not funded projects or achieved capabilities.
Submission deadlines and amendments can change and should be checked on the official notice.
